headline: Apollo Economist: AI Gives No Financial Payoff Outside Tech
script: AI has not helped the bottom line of big companies outside the tech industry. That is the finding of a recent note from Apollo Global Management's chief economist. Torsten Slok looks at what he calls the S&P 493. That means the S&P 500 minus seven big tech companies, including Apple, Amazon and Nvidia. He finds that profit margins and revenue per worker look flat. There is no evidence that AI is improving productivity at these companies. Slok says the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside tech. He is skeptical that non-tech companies are simply lagging behind the tech giants. He argues it will be tough to turn cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and profit margins. He writes that AI may be a great calculator, but in business intelligence is mostly judgment. He adds that AI does not understand accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs or fairness. Those things shape reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins. Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains.

terms.note: 指公司最终赚到的钱，也就是净利润。
指利润占收入的比例，反映赚钱效率。
指公司总收入除以员工人数，用来衡量效率。
指单位投入能产出多少，这里指员工创造的价值。
指标普500指数去掉七家大型科技公司后的493家。
